title: Add store buffers to the litmus model checker

blocks.text: This practice continues the previous one: the starter is its solution, with a second machine added. The baseline model can't explain what the team saw on an x86 server running in the interpreter: two threads that each wrote a flag and then read the other's both read 0, while a reader that saw a `ready` flag always saw the data written before it.

`outcomesWithStoreBuffers` models that server. Each thread's writes go into a buffer of its own and reach shared memory later, one at a time; at every step the checker tries both a thread's next operation and moving one buffered write to memory. A new operation, `fence()`, waits until the thread's own buffer is empty. Finish the three `TODO` methods of `Buffered` in `src/main/java/practice/LitmusModel.java`:

items: `load(t, variable)`: the value thread `t` reads now;
`canPerformNext(t)`: whether thread `t`'s next operation may run now;
`drainOne(t)`: a copy in which one of `t`'s buffered writes has reached memory.

blocks.text: When you're done, the checker allows both of the server's outcomes above and no outcome the server could not produce. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: two threads that each write one variable and then read the other's can end with any of the four combinations, both reads missing the writes included
a read in another thread can see a write or miss it
a thread that reads a variable it wrote gets its own latest write, even while that write is still buffered
with a fence between each thread's write and its read, the two reads can no longer both miss the other thread's write
a reader that sees a thread's second write also sees its first, because buffered writes reach memory in the order they were made

origin.section: The Processor's Store Buffer Lets a Read Overtake an Earlier Write, with No JIT at All

concepts: A full fence between a thread's write and its read rules out both reads missing the other thread's write.
A store waits in the core's store buffer, so a later load can complete first as seen by other cores, while the thread's own loads read its buffered writes; on x86 the buffer drains in order.
